ofdm_transceiver_top.summary: Mode-selectable OFDM transceiver top: TX / RX / internal loopback with frame wrap, RX input mux and on-chip BER checker.
ofdm_transceiver_top.header_comment:
ofdm_transceiver_top.v
MODE-SELECTABLE OFDM TRANSCEIVER TOP.

ONE design that, by a runtime mode[1:0] select, behaves as:

mode 0  TX        : data_bits_flat -> tx_ofdm_top -> tx_out_* master.
The RX chain is held idle (no input driven into it).

mode 1  RX        : ext_s_axis (raw 4160-sample sync-capable frame)
-> rx_full_chain_top -> m_bits_* demod master.
The TX is held idle (not started).

mode 2  LOOPBACK  : tx_ofdm_top -> internal 64+4032+64 = 4160 frame
wrap (the SAME framing proven in
tb/tx_rx_full_loopback_tb.sv, BER 0/10608)
-> rx_full_chain_top -> m_bits_* demod master,
plus rx_ber_checker for on-chip self-test BER.
No external I/O needed.

This wrapper instantiates ONLY frozen, independently-verified modules:
tx_ofdm_top        (frozen TX,  4032-sample slot, BER=0 standalone)
rx_full_chain_top  (frozen RX,  sync + FFT/CE/EQ/16QAM demod)
rx_ber_checker     (passive demod BER monitor)
Nothing inside those modules is modified.

TWO KEY MUXES
1. RX input mux:
rx_s_axis = (mode==LOOPBACK) ? tx_framed_stream : ext_s_axis
In TX mode the RX input is forced idle (tvalid=0), so an idle TX can
never inject into the RX.
2. TX output exposure:
tx_out_* carries the TX master in TX and LOOPBACK modes (the live
transmit stream). In RX mode the TX is not started, so tx_out is
idle.

LOOPBACK FRAMING (factored out of the proven TB)
The live TX emits a 4032-sample slot (m_last on 4031). In LOOPBACK the
wrapper captures that slot into a 4032-word buffer, then a small framing
FSM replays it into the RX S_AXIS as:
64 lead-in zeros | 4032 slot | 64 trailing zeros  = 4160 beats,
honoring rx s_axis_tready, asserting tlast on the final (4159th) beat.
This is byte-identical to golden/rx_downstream/tx_slot_iq.hex framing.

CONTROL
mode[1:0]      runtime mode select (0/1/2 as above).
start          1-cycle pulse: in TX/LOOPBACK kicks the TX slot (and, in
LOOPBACK, arms the framing replay once the slot is buffered).
ber_ctrl[31:0] rx_ber_checker control, board-mirrored layout:
bit0     = soft clear (level)
bit7:4   = status_sel (which BER counter to read)
bit11:8  = rot_off (0..11 whole-symbol ref rotation)
ber_status     selected rx_ber_checker counter (read total_bit_errors at
status_sel=0; the aligned rot_off reads 0).
The synchronizer enable / frame_len / threshold are configured through the
pass-through AXI4-Lite slave (regs 0x04 enable, 0x0C frame_len=4032,
0x68 threshold) exactly as rx_full_chain_top / the board top expect.

All control signals are plain top-level inputs here so the design is usable
directly (GPIO) OR by wiring mode/start/ber_ctrl to AXI-Lite/GPIO registers
in the board BD (documented; the board integration is the remaining step).

tx_ofdm_top.summary: OFDM transmitter top: emits one 4032-sample slot = 576-sample PSS/SSS sync preamble (ROM) + 12 data symbols from the QAM map -> IFFT -> CP chain.
tx_ofdm_top.header_comment:
tx_ofdm_top.v
OFDM TRANSMITTER integration TOP.  Builds ONE complete 4032-sample
transmit slot (the synchronizer's frame, minus the 64 pre/post zeros):

[ 2 REAL PSS/SSS sync symbols : 576 samples ]   (from sync ROM)
[ 12 data symbols x 288       : 3456 samples]   (TX chain below)
4032 samples   {Q,I} Q15

data path per symbol:
data bits (884) + pilot ROM (32 QPSK)
|
+---------v-----------+   16-QAM map + pilot insert + subcarrier
| tx_subcarrier_map   |   assembly + fftshift  -> 256 spectrum bins
+---------+-----------+
|  (fftshift-ordered spectrum, {Q,I})
+---------v-----------+   256-pt IDFT (xfft_N inverse, BFP) + 1/16
| tx_ifft_frontend    |   recover + CP insert  -> 288 time samples
+---------+-----------+
|  (288-sample data symbol, {Q,I} Q15)
v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
|  OUTPUT MUX : emit 576 sync ROM samples, then stream the 12 |
|  data symbols' 288-sample outputs back-to-back.             |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
v  m_axis  (4032 {Q,I} Q15, m_last on sample 4031)

Reproduces ref/transmitter.c generate_transmit_slot for the 14-symbol
slot and matches golden/rx_downstream/tx_slot_iq_4032.hex (the sync
region is byte-identical, the 12 data symbols within the IFFT BFP
truncation budget).

CONTROL / SEQUENCING
start (1-cycle pulse) kicks off a slot.  An FSM:
1. streams 576 sync ROM words to the master (SYNC phase),
2. for z = 0..11 : pulses sym_start to tx_subcarrier_map with the
z-th symbol's 884 data bits, lets the chain produce a 288-sample
symbol, and forwards those samples to the master (DATA phase).
The two stages of the data chain are pipelined-streaming, so once
started a symbol's spectrum bins flow continuously into the IFFT and
its time samples flow out; the FSM pulses sym_start for symbol z+1 as
soon as the mapper is free (it is double-buffered downstream).

Data bits source: a flat 12x884 bit memory `data_bits_flat`, provided
by the caller (TB loads golden tx_bits).  Pilot ROM: a 384-word
{Q,I} ROM streamed in pilot order (32/symbol) via pilot_tdata.

1 sample/clock, full AXI-Stream tready on the master.

rx_ber_checker.summary: Passive on-chip BER monitor: compares demod nibbles against a reference ROM with firmware-searchable whole-symbol rotation.
rx_ber_checker.header_comment:
rx_ber_checker.v   (ROBUST, FIRMWARE-ALIGNABLE rewrite)
ON-CHIP HARDWARE BIT-ERROR COUNTER for the full-RX demod output.

PURPOSE
Additive, NON-INTRUSIVE tap on rx_full_board_top's m_bits stream
(one 4-bit demod nibble per data subcarrier). It holds the known
2652-nibble golden reference for ONE frame in a ROM (loaded from
rx_ber_ref_rom.hex, generated from golden/rx_downstream/tx_bits.txt
with the SAME packing the demod emits: nibble = {b0,b1,b2,b3},
bit3=b0 .. bit0=b3), tracks the within-frame nibble position by
FREE-RUNNING from the first nibble after clear, compares each demod
nibble against ref[pos_eff], and accumulates:
total_bit_errors  - count of differing BITS across all checked frames
frames_checked    - number of COMPLETE frames checked (after warm-up)
total_nibbles     - number of nibbles checked (after warm-up)
plus an error-flag word (alignment / position sanity).

It is a pure passive monitor: it does NOT drive m_bits_tready or
touch any datapath signal. It snoops (m_bits_tvalid && m_bits_tready)
accepted beats only, so it is transparent to the verified RX chain.

POSITION / FRAME ALIGNMENT (ROBUST, firmware-search based)
The demod emits NDATA_SC (221) nibbles per OFDM symbol and NUM_DATA
(12) symbols per frame, in order, repeating every TOTAL_NIBBLES
(2652) nibbles. m_bits_tuser flags carrier 0 of a symbol;
m_bits_tlast flags carrier 220 of a symbol (symbol end).

The checker ANCHORS its OWN frame position at the FIRST m_bits beat
after clr -> that beat is symbol 0, carrier 0. It then FREE-RUNS:
- tuser  : carrier 0 of a symbol (resync nib_in_sym -> 0)
- tlast  : carrier 220 (symbol end); advance to next symbol,
wrapping symbol 11 -> 0 (the checker's frame boundary)
- else   : carrier++
pos_raw = sym_in_frame*NDATA_SC + nib_in_sym   (0..2651).

There is NO fragile pilot-ROM-wrap anchor anymore. The frame phase
relative to the golden reference frame is unknown (pipeline latency /
enable phase shift it by a whole number of symbols), so firmware sets
`rot_off` [3:0] (0..11) to ROTATE the REFERENCE index by whole symbols:
pos_eff = (pos_raw + rot_off*NDATA_SC) mod TOTAL_NIBBLES
One conditional subtract suffices because (pos_raw + rot_off*221) is
always < 2*2652. ref_nib = ref_rom[pos_eff]; the firmware simply
SEARCHES rot_off = 0..11 and the aligned value yields ~0 errors while
every other yields ~50%. This makes alignment immune to pipeline
latency / enable phase.

WARM-UP: the first frame seen after clr may be partial (the tap was
cleared mid-stream and the very first counted nibble might not be the
checker's frame-pos 0). We therefore do NOT count the first (warm-up)
frame: counting begins at the first FRAME BOUNDARY (symbol 11 -> 0)
after clr. frames_checked / total_nibbles / total_bit_errors only
accumulate from the first full frame onward. warmup_done / warmup_frames
are exposed so firmware can report the excluded frame.

STATUS / READBACK
All counters are exposed via a status_sel mux on status_data so one
32-bit input GPIO channel reads ALL counters.

tx_ifft_frontend.summary: 256-pt inverse FFT (xfft, BFP) + blk_exp recover with 1/16 scale + cyclic-prefix insertion -> 288-sample time symbol.
tx_ifft_frontend.header_comment:
tx_ifft_frontend.v
OFDM TX back-end: 256-pt IDFT (xfft_N driven INVERSE, BFP) + 1/16
recover scale + cyclic-prefix insert, producing one 288-sample
time-domain OFDM data symbol (CP + body), 1 sample/clock, AXI-Stream.

Ports ref/transmitter.c (ifft_new l.106 = FFTW_BACKWARD then /sqrt(NSC);
insert_cp l.108 = prepend last CP_LEN body samples) and matches the
validated rx_downstream_ref.tx_modulate_block IFFT+CP (CONTRACT.md
sec 4/5).

FFT IP  (rtl/xfft_N/xfft_N.xci -- a THIRD independent xfft_N instance;
the Meyr CFO core owns the first, rx_fft_frontend the second)
xfft 9.1, 256-pt, 16b I/Q, pipelined_streaming_io, natural order,
block_floating_point (BFP), truncation.  Configured INVERSE via
s_axis_config tdata bit0 FWD_INV = 0 (one-shot at reset).

NORMALIZATION
The C TX computes  body = FFTW_BACKWARD(spec) / sqrt(NSC).  FFTW_
BACKWARD is the UNSCALED inverse DFT = N * np.fft.ifft (a pure sum,
exp(+j2pi kn/N)).  The xfft inverse in BFP also computes that
unscaled inverse but right-shifts by a per-frame block exponent
`blk_exp` (m_axis_data_tuser, 8b) so the 16b output never overflows.
The TRUE unscaled inverse value is  ifft_true = out16 << blk_exp.
The golden applies the extra 1/sqrt(256) = 1/16 (>>4), so the body
sample this module emits is:

body_q15 = (out16 << blk_exp) >> 4        (per I and Q, rounded)

identical recover math to rx_fft_frontend.  (Verified vs the Python
golden: <= 2 LSB error per body sample, blk_exp ~= 3.)

CYCLIC PREFIX
insert_cp prepends the LAST CP_LEN=32 body samples to the front, so
the emitted 288-sample symbol is  body[224..255] , body[0..255].
The IFFT IP emits the 256 body samples in natural time order 0..255.
We buffer the whole symbol body (256x32 double-buffer) so we can read
out the CP (addresses 224..255) first, then the full body 0..255.
m_last marks the 288th (last) output sample of each symbol.

THROUGHPUT / TIMING
1 complex sample/clock everywhere; the input streams 256 spectrum
bins/symbol into the pipelined-streaming IFFT, which emits one body
sample/clock.  The BFP recover (barrel-shift + round + saturate) is
split into 2 registered stages, same as rx_fft_frontend, so the only
heavy arithmetic (the IFFT butterflies) lives in the Xilinx IP that
closes > 300 MHz OOC on this part.  Module Fmax (excl. IP) > 350 MHz.
Output is double-buffered (read symbol z while capturing z+1), so the
CP read-out never stalls between symbols.  Full AXI-Stream tready in
both directions.

tx_subcarrier_map.summary: Runtime-selectable QAM data mapper (QPSK..256QAM) + QPSK pilot insert + subcarrier assembly + fftshift into 256 spectrum bins.
tx_subcarrier_map.header_comment:
tx_subcarrier_map.v
OFDM TX front: runtime-selectable QAM data map + QPSK pilot insert +
subcarrier assembly + fftshift (rearrange_spectrum), producing the
256-bin frequency-domain spectrum (in IFFT-input / fftshift order)
for ONE data OFDM symbol, 1 bin / clock, AXI-Stream.

MULTI-MODULATION (mod_sel[1:0]):
0 = QPSK   (2 bits/sym, 1 bit/axis,  2 levels/axis: +/-1)
1 = 16-QAM (4 bits/sym, 2 bits/axis, 4 levels/axis: +/-1,3)
2 = 64-QAM (6 bits/sym, 3 bits/axis, 8 levels/axis: +/-1,3,5,7)
3 = 256QAM (8 bits/sym, 4 bits/axis, 16 levels/axis:+/-1..15)
k = bits/axis = mod_sel + 1 ;  nlev = 2^k levels/axis.

Per axis the k bits are FOLDED-GRAY coded:
bit[k-1] (MSB) = sign  (1 = positive amplitude)
bits[k-2:0]    = Gray code of the magnitude rank m (0 = innermost)
axis value = (+/- (2*m+1)) * SCALE_mod  ->  pre-scaled Q15 magnitude
taken from QAM_LVL[mod_sel][m] (exact rounded round((2m+1)*S*Q15)).
For mod_sel=1 (16-QAM) this is BIT-EXACT identical to the previous
fixed 16-QAM map (levels {1610,4829} = old Q16_1,Q16_3; axis code
{b_hi=sign, b_lo=gray(m)} = old tmp = b_hi*2+b_lo).

Per-mod SCALE = {1/sqrt(2),1/sqrt(10),1/sqrt(42),1/sqrt(170)} gives all
four constellations the SAME average symbol power (RMS-matched), with
the project Q15 spectrum scale 5090.697374.

DATA BITS INTERFACE
The caller presents the CURRENT symbol's data bits as a flat bus
`data_bits[NDATA_SC*BPC_MAX-1:0]` sized for the WIDEST mod (8 bits/
carrier).  For carrier k the BITS_PER_SYM = 2*k_axis bits live at
data_bits[k*BPC_MAX + b], b = 0 .. BITS_PER_SYM-1, in order
[a0 a1 .. a(K-1) | aq0 aq1 .. aq(K-1)] : first K bits = I axis
(a0 = MSB = sign), next K bits = Q axis. Unused high bits ignored.
Held stable for the whole symbol; latched at sym_start.

(For 16-QAM, BITS_PER_SYM=4, layout [b0 b1 b2 b3] = exactly the old
contract: b0,b1 = I axis (b0=sign), b2,b3 = Q axis.)

data bits / frame = NDATA_SC * (2*k) * NUM_DATA  (handled by caller).
Pilots STAY QPSK always (used by CE), streamed from the pilot ROM,
unchanged.

rx_full_chain_top__T9c40_CCz1.summary: Full RX integration: synchronizer (frame detect + timing + CFO) feeding the FFT/CE/EQ/demod downstream chain.
rx_full_chain_top__T9c40_CCz1.header_comment:
rx_full_chain_top.v
FULL-RX INTEGRATION — STEP 2 : SYNC -> FULL DOWNSTREAM (FFT/CE/EQ/DEMOD)
Step 1 (rx_full_top.v) proved the SYNC -> FFT front-end seam. This step
extends it to the COMPLETE downstream by attaching the existing,
independently-verified rtl/rx_downstream_top.v (BER=0 standalone)
directly to the synchronizer DUT's corrected M_AXIS.

DATA PATH
S_AXIS (raw IQ, {Q[31:16],I[15:0]} Q15, 4160-sample frame)
-> phase3_sync_axis_dma_wrapper   (frame detect + timing + CFO)
-> sync m_axis (4032-sample corrected slot, beat0 = PSS CP start)
-> rx_downstream_top
rx_fft_frontend  (skip 2 sync syms + per-sym CP, 256pt FFT
+ fftshift + 1/16)
-> rx_ch_est        (pilot-based CE + 32-tap interp_fft)
-> ping-pong RX-bin / H align buffer
-> rx_equalizer     (ZF: RX*conj(H)/|H|^2)
-> data-carrier gate (221 dataIndx bins)
-> rx_demod_16qam   (hard-slice 4 bits/carrier)
-> M_AXIS_BITS  (12 x 884 = 10608 demodulated bits)

NOTHING in the synchronizer, the downstream top, or the 4 downstream
modules is modified — this module ONLY instantiates the two frozen tops
(phase3_sync_axis_dma_wrapper + rx_downstream_top) and wires the plain
AXI-Stream seam between them.

SEAM TIMING NOTE (carried from step 1)
The sync DUT emits its corrected slot-1 sample EARLY (slot_start_index
= 63 vs the offset-free golden's 64) — a within-tolerance (+/-2) timing
quantization. This puts a 1-sample cyclic rotation (per-bin linear phase
ramp) on every FFT symbol. Step 1 confirmed it directly: the seam best-
aligns at offset -1 (sum|d| ~= 1008, essentially exact) and the FFT
magnitudes match the golden on 3036/3048 bins while I/Q rotate — a PURE
phase ramp, not a scale/ordering/timing bug. That ramp is absorbed by
the pilot-based channel estimation (the CE captures the 1-sample timing
phase as a 1-tap channel delay, well inside interp_fft's 32-tap budget)
and divided out by the ZF equalizer — exactly as the C reference handles
residual timing. The END-TO-END criterion is therefore demod BER vs the
offset-free golden bits, NOT a per-stage (FFT/H/EQ) bit-match.

The AXI-Lite slave and the sync debug taps are passed straight through
to this module's boundary so a TB can configure the regs and observe the
frame-detect / peak / slot-start indications exactly as the sync gates do.

phase3_sync_axis_dma_wrapper__pi1.summary: Synchronizer board wrapper: AXI4-Lite register file + AXI-Stream in/out around the sync core, frame-length tlast generation.
phase3_sync_axis_dma_wrapper__pi1.header_comment:
phase3_sync_axis_dma_wrapper — P3-14B
Board-integration wrapper: wraps phase3_sync_top with AXI-Lite control/status
registers, enable gating, soft reset, replay buffer, integer CFO correction,
input/output counters, TLAST generation, bypass mode, and wrapper-level error flags.

P3-14B additions over P3-14A:
- iq_replay_buffer_576: captures frac-corrected IQ during frame run
- nco_phase_gen (u_int_nco): integer CFO step word → sin/cos
- complex_rotator (u_int_rot): applies integer correction to replayed IQ
- M_AXIS now carries fully corrected (frac + integer) IQ stream
- INT_CFO_APPLIED and INT_CFO_INDEX registers fully wired
- Start re-arm deferred until replay_done (prevents capture collision)

Pipeline (non-bypass):
S_AXIS → phase3_sync_top (frac corr + Meyr) → replay buffer (capture)
↓ (after Meyr done)
replay buffer → integer NCO + rotator → M_AXIS (DMA)

Enable gate:
enable=0 → s_axis_tready=0, m_axis_tvalid=0.
enable=1 → normal or bypass mode.

Bypass mode (bypass_enable=1):
S_AXIS passes directly to M_AXIS. DUT and replay buffer receive no data.

Start/done/replay protocol:
After dut_aresetn rising edge: start_armed=1 → start fires.
After meyr_done (int_cfo_valid): replay_start fires; replay buffer plays back.
After replay_done: start_armed=1 (re-arm for next frame).
After error (done && error):  start_armed=0; wait for soft_reset.

TLAST generation:
Counter-based M_AXIS TLAST, counter period = FRAME_LEN_SAMPLES register (default 4032
for the 14-symbol slot; NUM_DATA_BLOCKS=12 plus PSS+SSS pair).
The replay buffer outputs exactly FRAME_LEN beats per replay, so the counter
fires naturally on each replay cycle.

INT_CFO_APPLIED:
Sticky bit; set when replay_busy first asserts. Cleared by dut_aresetn.

rx_downstream_top__CCz1.summary: RX downstream: FFT frontend -> channel estimate -> RX/H align -> ZF equalizer -> data-carrier gate -> QAM demapper.
rx_downstream_top__CCz1.header_comment:
rx_downstream_top.v
OFDM RX DOWNSTREAM integration TOP.  Wires the 4 verified, golden-
validated, timing-closed downstream modules into one AXI-Stream chain:

(sync M_AXIS, 4032 {Q,I} Q15)
|
+---------v----------+
|  rx_fft_frontend   |  symbol-extract + 256pt FFT + fftshift + 1/16
+---------+----------+  -> 12 x 256 freq bins, fftshift order, {Q,I}
|  (FX[i], i=bin 0..255, m_last on bin 255)
+----------------------------+
|                            |
+---------v----------+        +--------v--------------------------+
|   rx_ch_est        |        |  RX-BIN ALIGN BUFFER (ping-pong)  |
|  (CE + interp_fft) |        |  256x32 x2 : stores FX symbol s,  |
|  + pilot_rom       |        |  replays it bin-by-bin in lockstep|
+---------+----------+        |  with the matching H symbol s     |
|  (H[i], 12x256)   +--------+--------------------------+
|                            |
|  H stream  ----------------+----  (drives the read of the
|                            |       align buffer: the EQ
+---------v----------------------------v--------+ consumes RX[i] and
|              rx_equalizer (ZF)                 | H[i] for the SAME
|   eq[i] = RX[i]*conj(H[i]) / |H[i]|^2          | symbol/bin together
+---------+-------------------------------------+
|  (eq[i], all 256 bins, TUSER = bin index 0..255)
+---------v----------+
|  DATA-CARRIER GATE |  keep only the 221 dataIndx bins (ascending);
|  (dataIndx mask)   |  drop pilots / DC / bins 0,255.
+---------+----------+
|  (12 x 221 equalized data carriers)
+---------v----------+
|  rx_demod_16qam    |  hard-slice -> 4 bits/carrier
+---------+----------+
|  m_bits[3:0], m_last on carrier 220 of each symbol
v   (12 x 884 bits)

ALIGNMENT SCHEME  (the core integration concern)
rx_ch_est has SYMBOL-GRANULARITY latency: it must collect a whole
symbol's 256 bins (to capture the 32 pilots), then run the interp MAC
pipeline, before the FIRST H bin of that symbol appears.  The matching
RX freq bins emerge from the FFT front-end MUCH earlier.  So the EQ
cannot just be fed FX and H from the two source streams directly --
they are skewed by (at least) one whole symbol.

Fix: a ping-pong RX-bin buffer.  The FFT front-end's m_axis FX stream
is FORKED:
(a) into rx_ch_est  (which derives H), and
(b) into a 256x32 ping-pong RAM that stores every FX symbol.
The H stream out of rx_ch_est is the MASTER of the equalizer feed: for
every H beat (symbol s, bin b, in order 0..255) we read the SAME (s,b)
FX word back out of the align buffer and present BOTH to the EQ on the
same cycle.  The two EQ inputs are therefore bin-for-bin, symbol-for-
symbol aligned by construction, independent of the exact ch_est
latency.  Because ch_est emits exactly one ordered 0..255 H symbol per
stored FX symbol, the buffer's write/read symbol pointers track each
other with a 2-deep ping-pong (capture symbol s+1 while H of symbol s
is read out).

phase3_axi_lite_regs.summary: AXI4-Lite slave register file (control/status/frame-len/debug/error registers) for the synchronizer.
phase3_axi_lite_regs.header_comment:
phase3_axi_lite_regs — P3-14A
AXI4-Lite slave register bank for Phase3 OFDM synchronizer wrapper.
Derived from phase2_axi_lite_regs.v (P2-14/P2-18/P2-20D/P2-20E).

Register map (byte addresses, 32-bit words, ADDR_WIDTH=7):
0x00 VERSION           [31:0] R,  constant 0x00316001
0x04 CONTROL           [1:0]  bit0=enable(R/W), bit1=soft_reset_pulse(W1S, reads 0)
0x08 STATUS            [7:0]  bit0=busy(live), bit1=done_seen(W1C), bit2=error_seen(W1C)
bit[7:4]=last_error_code (latched on error completion)
0x0C FRAME_LEN_SAMPLES [11:0] R/W, default=4032 (14*(NSC+CP_LEN)), range 1-4095
0x10 INPUT_COUNT       [31:0] R
0x14 OUTPUT_COUNT      [31:0] R
0x18 FRAME_START_VALID [0]    R/clear — sticky latch; read clears
Set by frame_start_valid_i. No snapshot trigger.
0x1C FRAME_START_INDEX [11:0] R, latched on frame_start_valid_i (or snapshot)
0x20 PEAK_INDEX        [8:0]  R, latched on frame_start_valid_i (or snapshot)
0x24 SLOT_START_INDEX  [11:0] R, latched on slot_start_valid_i (or snapshot)
0x28 FRAC_CFO_VALID    [0]    R/clear — sticky latch; read clears
0x2C FRAC_CFO_PHASE    [31:0] R, Q1.15 frac CFO word sign-extended 16->32 (or snapshot)
0x30 PSS_DONE          [0]    R/clear — sticky; TODO: not yet wired
0x34 SSS_DONE          [0]    R/clear — sticky; TODO: not yet wired
0x38 INT_CFO_VALID     [0]    R/clear — sticky latch; read clears; set by int_cfo_valid_i.
Reading with latch=1 triggers snapshot of all sync results.
0x3C INT_CFO_EST       [31:0] R, 32-bit NCO step word from dbg_integer_cfo_word (or snapshot)
0x40 INT_CFO_INDEX     [8:0]  R, Meyr peak index latched on int_cfo_valid_i (or snapshot)
0x44 INT_CFO_APPLIED   [0]    R, sticky from wrapper replay_busy first-assert (or snapshot)
0x48 RESET_STATUS      [1:0]  bit0=RESET_DONE(sticky W1C), bit1=PIPELINE_IDLE(live)
0x4C DEBUG_CONTROL     [3:0]  bit0=BYPASS_ENABLE(R/W), bit1=FORCE_TLAST(self-clear),
bit2=COUNTER_CLEAR(self-clear), bit3=DEBUG_MODE(R/W)
0x50 TLAST_COUNT       [31:0] R, from tlast_count_i
0x54 ERROR_FLAGS       [3:0]  sticky W1C: bit0=FRAME_LEN_MISMATCH, bit1=TLAST_TIMEOUT,
bit2=RESET_WHILE_ACTIVE, bit3=STALL_TIMEOUT
0x58 INPUT_PERIOD      [12:0] R/W, player input period (default 4160)
0x5C CYC_TOTAL_CNT     [31:0] R, free-running cycle counter (measurement-window denom)
0x60 IN_TVALID_CNT     [31:0] R, cycles s_axis_tvalid asserted (player presenting)
0x64 IN_TREADY_CNT     [31:0] R, cycles s_axis_tready asserted (DUT ready)
(cleared on !dut_aresetn or COUNTER_CLEAR, like INPUT_COUNT)
other: SLVERR

Snapshot protocol:
When SW reads 0x38 (INT_CFO_VALID) while latch=1:
- Seven sync result registers frozen simultaneously into shadow registers.
- While snapshot_valid=1, reads of 0x1C/0x20/0x24/0x2C/0x3C/0x40/0x44 return shadow values,
keeping INT_CFO_EST / INT_CFO_INDEX / INT_CFO_APPLIED coherent in a single AXI sequence.

Note on frame_start_valid_i timing:
dbg_frame_start_valid, dbg_peak_valid, and dbg_frac_cfo_valid all fire on the same
cycle (frac_frac_phase_valid) in phase3_sync_top. The wrapper passes one pulse as
frame_start_valid_i to this module, which latches all three fields simultaneously.

rx_demod_qam.summary: Hard-decision QAM demapper (QPSK..256QAM), folded-Gray axis slicing, MSB-first bit packing.
rx_demod_qam.header_comment:
rx_demod_qam.v
OFDM RX downstream chain: runtime-selectable QAM hard-decision
demodulator (QPSK / 16-QAM / 64-QAM / 256-QAM).  Generalizes the old
rx_demod_16qam.v threshold slicer to 2^(k) levels per axis.

MULTI-MODULATION (mod_sel[1:0]):
0 = QPSK   (1 bit/axis,  2 levels/axis)
1 = 16-QAM (2 bits/axis, 4 levels/axis)   <- bit-exact to old core
2 = 64-QAM (3 bits/axis, 8 levels/axis)
3 = 256QAM (4 bits/axis,16 levels/axis)
K = bits/axis = mod_sel+1 ; nlev = 2^K levels/axis.

Per axis (input v, signed Q15):
sign = (v >= 0)                  -> axis MSB
m    = min( |v| / STEP_mod , nlev/2-1 )   (magnitude rank)
axis bits = { sign , gray(m) }   (folded-Gray; exact inverse of
tx_subcarrier_map qam_axis).
STEP_mod = round(2*SCALE_mod*Q15) = level spacing in Q15:
QPSK 7199 , 16QAM 3220 , 64QAM 1571 , 256QAM 781.
|v|/STEP is done with a small unrolled comparator ladder (no divide).

16-QAM (mod_sel=1) reproduces the old rx_demod_16qam EXACTLY:
per axis v<=-TH:01 v<0:00 v<+TH:10 else:11  (TH=STEP=3220), and
m_bits[3:0] = {I_axis(b0,b1), Q_axis(b2,b3)}.

Output bit packing m_bits[BPC_MAX-1:0] (BPC_MAX=8):
m_bits[K-1:0]   = I axis bits  (m_bits[K-1] = MSB = sign)
m_bits[2K-1:K]  = Q axis bits  (m_bits[2K-1] = MSB = sign)
high unused bits = 0. Active bit count BITS_PER_SYM = 2*K.
(For 16-QAM: m_bits[3:0] = [b0 b1 b2 b3] identical to old port.)

THROUGHPUT/TIMING: identical single registered stage / valid-ready
handshake / back-pressure as the old core (comparator-only, no mult).

rx_equalizer.summary: Zero-forcing equalizer: X = Y * conj(H) / |H|^2 using a reciprocal LUT divider.
rx_equalizer.header_comment:
rx_equalizer.v  — AXI-Stream zero-forcing equalizer (top wrapper)
Streams freq-domain RX symbols and the channel estimate H, one complex
sample per clock, and produces the equalized symbols

eq[i] = RX[i] * conj(H[i]) / |H[i]|^2          (ZF, receiver.c fde)

at 1 sample/clk, back-to-back, fully pipelined. Guards |H|^2 == 0 -> 0.

INTERFACE (one 32-bit beat = one complex sample, {Q[31:16], I[15:0]}):
* s_axis_rx   : RX freq-domain sample (TDATA = {rxQ,rxI})
* s_axis_h    : channel estimate H    (TDATA = {hQ ,hI })  (Q15;
H is sign-extended to 18b inside the divider)
* s_axis_*_tuser : carries the bin index (0..255) for downstream
carrier extraction; passed straight through.
* m_axis      : equalized sample (TDATA = {eqQ,eqI}); TUSER = bin idx.

Both input streams advance together: a transfer happens only when
BOTH s_axis_rx_tvalid and s_axis_h_tvalid are high and the pipeline
is allowed to advance. Backpressure (m_axis_tready low while the
output is occupied) freezes the whole pipeline via a common clock
enable, so NO samples are dropped and throughput is 1/clk whenever
downstream is ready. The intrinsic latency is the divider depth (9).

(Carrier extraction to the 221 dataIndx bins is a downstream concern;
this module equalizes every bin and tags it with TUSER so the next
stage / TB can keep only the data carriers. The accompanying TB
performs exactly that extraction and checks against eq_out.hex.)

Synthesizable Verilog-2001. Target part: xczu49dr-ffvf1760-2-e.

rx_fft_frontend.summary: Skips sync symbols + per-symbol CP, 256-pt forward FFT (xfft, BFP), blk_exp recover with 1/16 scale + fftshift.
rx_fft_frontend.header_comment:
rx_fft_frontend.v
OFDM RX downstream chain: FFT FRONT-END (symbol extract + 256-pt FFT
+ fftshift + 1/sqrt(256) scale).  Ports the RX FFT stage of
ref/receiver.c (generate_complex_symbol + fft_with_rearrange),
matching golden/rx_downstream/fft_out (see CONTRACT.md sec 3.1).

WHAT IT DOES  (CONTRACT.md sec 3.1)
INPUT  : the synchronizer's corrected M_AXIS, 32-bit {Q[31:16],
I[15:0]} signed Q15, 1 complex sample / clock, 4032
samples / slot, beat0 = PSS CP start.
- samples   0..575  : 2 REAL sync symbols (PSS/SSS) -> SKIPPED
(used by sync, never demodulated here).
- data sym z (0..11): samples 576 + z*288 .. +287.
For each of the 12 data symbols:
1. drop the 32-sample cyclic prefix,
2. take the next NSC=256 body samples,
3. 256-pt forward FFT (exp(-j2pi kn/N)),
4. rearrange_spectrum / fftshift (cyclic rotate by NSC/2=128),
5. scale by 1/sqrt(256) = 1/16 (4-bit right shift).
OUTPUT : 12 symbols x 256 complex freq bins, fftshift-ordered
(bin 0..255 within a symbol, symbols 0..11 consecutively),
AXI-Stream {Q[31:16],I[15:0]} Q15, 1 sample / clock.
-> matches golden/rx_downstream/fft_out.hex.

FFT IP  (rtl/xfft_N/xfft_N.xci -- instantiated here as a SECOND,
INDEPENDENT instance; the Meyr CFO core owns the first one)
xfft 9.1, 256-pt, 16b I/Q, pipelined_streaming_io, natural order,
block_floating_point (BFP), truncation. Configured FORWARD via
s_axis_config tdata bit0 FWD_INV=1 (one-shot at reset).

BLOCK-FLOATING-POINT HANDLING
In BFP the IP performs an UNSCALED forward FFT but right-shifts the
data by a per-frame "block exponent" (reported on m_axis_data_tuser,
8 bits) so the 16b output never overflows. The TRUE unscaled FFT
value is therefore  fft_true = out16 << blk_exp.
The golden applies the extra 1/sqrt(256)=1/16 (>>4), so the value
this module must emit is:

bin_q15 = (out16 << blk_exp) >> 4          (per I and Q)

= out16 << (blk_exp-4) when blk_exp>=4, else out16 >> (4-blk_exp)
with round-to-nearest on the right shift. This is the EXACT inverse
of whatever scaling the IP chose, so the result is independent of
the actual blk_exp value -- only BFP intermediate truncation (a few
LSB) separates it from the bit-exact golden. The recover shift is
done at full width (32b) before re-saturating to int16, so no
intermediate clipping. (Verified: emulated 256-pt BFP gives blk_exp
~= 2 and <= 0.7 LSB recovered error vs the golden Q15 view.)

THROUGHPUT / SAMPLING RATE / TIMING  (user hard constraints)
* 1 complex sample / clock everywhere; the symbol-extract FSM feeds
the pipelined-streaming FFT one body sample per clock and the IP
emits one bin per clock -> NO rate change (no decimate/interp).
* Honors AXI-Stream tready in BOTH directions:
- upstream s_axis is back-pressured by s_ready, which is only
asserted when the sample is a SKIP (sync/CP, always accepted)
or the FFT data slave can accept a body sample.
- downstream m_axis is back-pressured: the fftshift read-out
buffer holds a whole symbol, and read pointer only advances on
(m_valid & m_ready); a full output buffer back-pressures the

phase3_sync_top__T9c40.summary: Synchronizer orchestrator FSM: timing sync (CP autocorr + frame detect), Meyr integer-CFO core, fractional-CFO estimate/correct.
phase3_sync_top__T9c40.header_comment:
phase3_sync_top.v  (P5-02 L2 rewire)

Replaces the old serial-Meyr pipeline with the new FFT-corr core.

Internal pipeline (all live on the frac-corrected stream — no
internal replay path):

s_axis_*
│
▼
frac_cfo_frame_corrector_top  (u_frac_corr)
│  frac_m_*  (frac-corrected IQ + tlast)
▼

rx_ch_est__WBz1.summary: Pilot-based channel estimation: Hp = rx * W (precomputed conj(p)/|p|^2) + 32-tap interp-FFT interpolation to all bins.
rx_ch_est__WBz1.header_comment:
rx_ch_est.v  --  OFDM RX channel estimation + FFT interpolation (CE + interp_fft)

Ports receiver.c ch_estimation_fdm() + interp_fft() to RTL.

(1) ch_estimation_fdm : at each of the 32 pilot bins pltIndx={1,9,...,249}
H_pilot[k] = rx[pltIndx[k]] * conj(plt[k]) / |plt[k]|^2
The transmitted QPSK pilot plt[k] is KNOWN, so the per-pilot reciprocal
W[k] = conj(plt[k]) / |plt[k]|^2  (at Q15 scale)
is a PRECOMPUTED complex CONSTANT. The CE is therefore a single complex
H_pilot[k] = rx[pltIndx[k]] * W[k]
MULTIPLY -- no run-time divide. This is mathematically identical to the
old 64-bit single-cycle complex divide (655 logic levels, ~77 ns, could
not close timing), so golden hest.hex is UNCHANGED (0 LSB on golden, the
same 0-3 LSB budget on the 24 robust channels). W is loaded from
W_RECIP_ROM (golden/rx_downstream/ce_pilot_recip.hex, 384 = 12*32 words,
{Wi[17:0],Wr[17:0]}, 16 frac bits) via $readmemh, addressed by the same
pilot pull counter that advances pilot_tready (slot-major k=0..31 inner).

(2) interp_fft : 32-pt IFFT of the 32 pilot-H into the low 32 time taps,
zero taps[32:256], 256-pt forward FFT -> H_fft[0..255].
Because taps[32:256]==0, the WHOLE interp_fft is LINEAR in the 32 pilot
inputs and collapses to a single fixed 256x32 complex matrix W:
H_fft[k] = sum_{m=0..31} W[k][m] * H_pilot[m]
W = DFT256[:,0:32] @ (IDFT32 / 32)
W is stored in rtl/rx_ch_est_rom/ce_interp_W.hex (18-bit signed, 16
fractional bits). This avoids any FFT IP, is fully pipelined, and is the
cheapest path to timing closure (no feedback, pure MAC adder-tree).

(3) +1 offset (receiver.c l.152-153): Hest[1..254] = H_fft[0..253];
Hest[0] = Hest[255] = 0. Implemented by only computing H_fft[0..253]
and writing them to output bins 1..254, with bins 0/255 forced 0.

I/O: AXI-Stream, ONE complex sample / clock, {Q[31:16], I[15:0]} Q15
(scale 5090.70 -> H=1.0 reads ~0x13E3). tready honored.

Throughput: 1 sample/clk sustained. Input symbol N+1 captured into the
alternate pilot bank while output symbol N streams (ping-pong) -> no bubble.

Pipelining (timing closure): CE divide spread over the 256-cycle symbol
(only 32 pilots). The interp MAC is a fully-registered 32-wide complex
multiply + 5-level balanced adder tree (9-stage fixed latency, 1 bin/clk),
so each pipeline stage is a single multiply or a single add -> short logic
depth, no feedback paths.

meyr_cfo_top.summary: Meyr FFT-correlation integer-CFO core: ak FFT -> zero-pad -> 2N FFT x conj(B[k]) ROM -> IFFT -> peak -> k_int.
meyr_cfo_top.header_comment:
meyr_cfo_top.v

Complete Meyr Integer CFO Estimation Pipeline

DATAPATH (all pipelined, no FSM):
PSS/SSS time-domain input
→ meyr_feeder → xfft_N (N-pt FFT, BFP)
→ meyr_Rm_dut
→ meyr_FFT_ak_dut (A[k] + zero-pad)
→ xfft_2N (2N-pt FFT, BFP)
→ ROM × (conj(FFT(B[k])))
→ meyr_ifft_peak_dut
→ xfft_IFFT (2N-pt IFFT, BFP)
→ Peak power search
→ cfo_int output

CONFIG:
All three FFT IPs are configured by one-shot latches
immediately after reset. No external config interface
needed - the module is self-initializing.

ROM:
conj(FFT(B[k])) is stored in inferred BRAM inside
meyr_Rm_dut. For simulation, load via hierarchical
$readmemh from the TB. For synthesis, add
initial $readmemh("bk_conj_fft512_rom.txt", rom);
inside meyr_Rm_dut, or replace with BRAM IP + .coe.

PARAMETERS:
N      : subcarrier count (PSS/SSS length)
FFT_2N : correlation FFT size (2*N)

TIMING at 250 MHz, N=256:
End-to-end latency: ~3742 cycles = ~14.97 µs

meyr_slot_frontend.summary: Extracts the sync-symbol region of the slot for the Meyr correlator.
meyr_slot_frontend.header_comment:
meyr_slot_frontend.v

Pipelined Slot Demux for OFDM Receiver Front-End

PURPOSE:
Sits between ADC/timing-sync and meyr_cfo_top.
Accepts raw continuous sample stream + slot_start pulse,
strips CPs, routes PSS/SSS to Meyr estimator.

SLOT STRUCTURE (from OFDM.h):
NUM_SYN  = 2 (PSS, SSS)
NUM_DATA = 12 (data symbols, 5G NR: 14 total - 2 sync)
Each symbol = CP_LEN + N samples
Total slot  = (NUM_SYN + NUM_DATA) * (CP_LEN + N)

[CP+PSS][CP+SSS][CP+D0][CP+D1]...[CP+D11]
sym 0   sym 1   sym 2  sym 3     sym 13

OPERATION:
1. Wait for slot_start pulse from timing sync
2. Count through entire slot
3. During CP regions: suppress output (tvalid=0)
4. During PSS/SSS payload: assert meyr_tvalid
5. During data payload: assert data_tvalid

ARCHITECTURE:
Pure counter logic. No FSM, no BRAM, no buffering.
1-cycle registered pipeline for clean timing.

INTERFACE WITH Fractional CFO BLOCK:
slot_start is a single-cycle pulse indicating sample 0
of a new slot has arrived on s_tdata in this cycle.
Typically generated by CP autocorrelation peak detector
(Van de Beek method).

meyr_sync_capture.summary: Captures the 576-sample sync region into RAM for Meyr processing.
meyr_sync_capture.header_comment:
meyr_sync_capture.v

PURPOSE:
Bridge between meyr_slot_frontend (continuous payload stream)
and meyr_cfo_top (AXI-Stream consumer that occasionally
deasserts s_tready while reconfiguring its non-realtime FFTs).
Buffers 2N samples (PSS payload + SSS payload), then streams
them into the core with proper handshake.

GUARANTEES:
- Write side ALWAYS accepts (downstream never drops a sample);
slot_frontend output is gated to land inside the buffer.
- Read side honors core.out_tready strictly.
- PSS-then-SSS order preserved by linear write addressing.
- r1_pending is driven from a SINGLE always-block (this module's
capture FSM) — no race between estimator-side and ingest-side.

STORAGE / READ-PATH:
Inferred small RAM (2N x DATA_W). Read is combinational so a
single output register on the consumer side delivers 1 beat /
cycle without an internal skid buffer. For 256-subcarrier
config 2N x 32 = 16 Kbit which Vivado maps to distributed RAM
(LUTRAM). Switch the ram_style attribute to "block" if the
parameter pushes the capacity past LUTRAM density.

OVERRUN POLICY:
If pss_first_beat fires while a previous capture has not been
drained, overrun_event pulses for one cycle and the new
capture replaces the in-flight one. Documented "newest-PSS
wins" policy: guarantees forward progress on bursty slot
starts and keeps the integer-CFO estimate aligned to the most
recent slot.

rx_eq_complex_div.summary: Complex divide by |H|^2 via reciprocal lookup + Newton-Raphson refinement.
rx_eq_complex_div.header_comment:
rx_eq_complex_div.v
Zero-forcing equalizer complex divider core (per-subcarrier).

eq[i] = RX[i] * conj(H[i]) / |H[i]|^2

num_i = Ri*Hi + Rq*Hq          (real part of RX*conj(H))
num_q = Rq*Hi - Ri*Hq          (imag part of RX*conj(H))
sc    = Hi*Hi + Hq*Hq          (= |H|^2)
eq    = (num_i + j*num_q) / sc

All operands are signed Q15 integers at golden scale S = 5090.697374
(float 1.0 -> 0x13E3). The golden output hex is eq_float * S, so the
datapath computes:  eq_int = round( num / sc * S ).

DIVIDER ARCHITECTURE (most timing-critical op in the chain):
* reciprocal of |H|^2 via normalize + 7-bit LUT seed + TWO
Newton-Raphson refinements  r <- r*(2 - x*r).
* |H|^2 is normalized into [2^30, 2^31) by a leading-zero shift
(sh = 31 - bitlength(sc)); reciprocal of the mantissa is computed
in Q18, then denormalized by the same shift in the final stage.
* Worst-case relative reciprocal error 3.8e-6 over the FULL 32-bit
|H|^2 dynamic range (verified) -> robust for small |H| as well.
* Fully registered, one complex sample per clock, back-to-back.

Guard: sc == 0  ->  output 0 (band-edge / unpopulated bins).

PIPELINE DEPTH: 12 stages (input reg -> output reg). LATENCY = 12 clk.
S1 input | S2 products | S3 sums(num,|H|^2) | S4 normalize+LUT seed |
S5a,S5b Newton iter-1 | S6a,S6b Newton iter-2 | S7 *S | S8 *recip |
S9a denorm-shift+round | S9b saturate+zero-guard.  Each NR iteration
is split so every clock does at most ONE DSP multiply, and the
variable barrel-shift is separated from saturation -- those two
structures were the Fmax limiters.
A 12-deep "valid" shift register carries the strobe; tuser passes
through for downstream bin/carrier tagging.

Synthesizable Verilog-2001. No vendor primitives, no IP.
Target part: xczu49dr-ffvf1760-2-e.

slot_start_controller.summary: Generates the corrected slot-start alignment from the detected peak.
slot_start_controller.header_comment:
slot_start_controller — Phase 3 glue

Latches slotStartIndex = frame_index + peak_lag from frac_cfo_frame_corrector_top
when its done pulse fires.  Provides the constant PSS and SSS FFT window
start addresses (relative to the corrected output stream) for
pss_sss_symbol_extractor.

C reference (receiver.c:291):
slotStartIndex = peakIndexAuto + frameStart

RTL mapping:
frame_index  = frameStart     (BUF_AW-bit buffer address)
peak_lag     = peakIndexAuto  (INDEX_WIDTH-bit offset from frameStart)
slot_start   = frame_index + peak_lag

Corrected IQ output from frac_cfo_frame_corrector_top starts at slot_start.
Therefore, within that output stream, the PSS and SSS FFT windows are:
pss_fft_start = CP_LEN
sss_fft_start = 2*CP_LEN + NSC
frame_len     = 2*(NSC + CP_LEN)   (required OUTPUT_SAMPLES of corrector)

All three PSS/SSS parameters are constants derived from NSC/CP_LEN and are
provided as registered outputs for clean fanout.

slot_valid is a 1-cycle pulse synchronized to done_in; it remains asserted
for exactly one clock and is re-armed on each done_in pulse.

frac_cfo_frame_corrector_top__pi2.summary: Frame-buffered fractional-CFO corrector: replays the captured frame through the rotator.
frac_cfo_frame_corrector_top__pi2.header_comment:
frac_cfo_frame_corrector_top: AXI-Stream capture → frame detection →
CP timing sync → fractional CFO estimation → fractional CFO correction.

Integrates (all sharing one iq_frame_buffer via FSM-muxed read port):
iq_frame_buffer      — AXI-Stream fill + random-access read
frame_detector       — sliding-window energy frame start
timing_frac_cfo_top  — CP autocorr + timing metric + CORDIC atan2
frac_cfo_corrector_top — NCO + complex_rotator (frac CFO removal)

C reference (synchronization()):
frame_index  = frame_detector(...)
peak_lag     = VanDeBeekAutoCorrelation(...)
frac_phase   = -atan2(Q[peak_lag], I[peak_lag]) / (2π) [Q1.15]
corrected[n] = raw[slot_start+n] × exp(-j·2π·frac_phase·n)

slot_start = frame_index + peak_lag (CP start, timing-corrected)
Output: TOTAL_SAMPLES = NSC+CP_LEN corrected IQ samples, tlast on last.

NCO step word: step = -frac_phase × 2^8  [A-FIX2]
frac_phase Q1.15: per-symbol total phase. Per-sample step = phase / NSC (NSC=256=2^8).
step = sign_ext({-frac_phase, 8'b0})

NCO sequencing in S_LOAD_NCO (counted by nco_cnt, combinatorial decode):
nco_cnt=0: load_step=1 (latch step_word into NCO)
nco_cnt=1: phase_reset=1 (clear NCO accumulator)
nco_cnt=2..LATENCY+1: enable=1, wait for sincos_valid
nco_cnt=LATENCY+2: sincos_valid high → enter S_CORRECT

Buffer playback (S_CORRECT): 1-cycle registered read latency, 1-deep hold
FIFO with back-pressure from m_axis.  can_issue fires when hold is free
(or being freed) and a pending read is not outstanding.
Throughput: 1 sample per 2 clocks (limited by buffer latency pipeline).

done fires 1 clock after last corrector-input sample is accepted.
Since axis_complex_mult has 1-cycle output latency, m_axis_tlast fires
at the same clock as done (when m_axis_tready=1 throughout S_CORRECT).

FSM: IDLE → FILL → FRAME_DET → TIMING_CFO → LOAD_NCO → CORRECT → DONE

frac_cfo_corrector_top.summary: Applies the fractional-CFO correction: NCO phase + complex rotation of the sample stream.
frac_cfo_corrector_top.header_comment:
frac_cfo_corrector_top: integrates nco_phase_gen + complex_rotator.

Programs the NCO with a pre-computed step word (step = round(-frac_phase × 2^32 / 2π))
and rotates each IQ sample by exp(-j*theta[n]).

Caller must:
1. Assert load_step with the desired step_word for 1 cycle.
2. Assert phase_reset for 1 cycle to clear the phase accumulator.
3. Assert enable.  sincos_valid goes high exactly LATENCY clocks later.
4. Begin sending IQ samples only after sincos_valid is high.

frame_frac_cfo_top.summary: Combines frame timing with fractional-CFO estimation over the detected frame.
frame_frac_cfo_top.header_comment:
frame_frac_cfo_top: CP timing synchronization + fractional CFO estimation.

Frozen-architecture wrapper encapsulating:
timing_sync_top    — Schmidl-Cox autocorr peak detection (streaming_cp_autocorr + peak_detector)
frac_cfo_estimator — CORDIC atan2 for fractional CFO phase

External interface is identical to timing_frac_cfo_top; frac_cfo_frame_corrector_top
instantiates this module as u_tfc.

FSM: S_IDLE → S_TIMING → S_FRAC_CFO → S_DONE

iq_capture_pingpong.header_comment:
iq_capture_pingpong.v   (H1a — continuous multi-slot front-end)

PURPOSE
Decouple AXI-Stream acquisition from the (slow) frac+meyr processing so the
sync chain can run CONTINUOUS back-to-back slots without going deaf. Owns
the AXI ingest port and TWO iq_frame_buffer instances (A/B) in ping-pong:
one buffer captures slot N+1 while the other is being processed for slot N.

s_axis_tready stays HIGH as long as at least one buffer is free; it drops
only when BOTH buffers hold un-processed frames (processing fell behind —
the expected ~50% duty backpressure, since frac S_CORRECT is ~2 clk/sample).

ALIGNMENT
Each capture ends on s_axis_tlast (NOT buffer-full) because DEPTH (2^CAP_AW
= 8192) >= the stim frame (4160). So every buffer holds exactly one whole,
correctly-bounded frame -> the downstream frame_detector / slot arithmetic
line up identically slot-to-slot.

HANDOFF PROTOCOL (to the processing FSM in frac_cfo_frame_corrector_top)
buf_ready : level — the next-in-order captured buffer is waiting + proc idle
buf_len   : sample_count of that ready buffer
proc_take : 1-cyc — processor claims the ready buffer (latches proc_sel)
proc_free : 1-cyc — processor done; buffer returns to the free pool
rd_en/rd_addr/rd_data : random-access read of the buffer the processor owns

Capture order (A,B,A,B,...) == process order (A,B,A,B,...) so the two
cap_sel / proc_next pointers each just toggle; with 2 buffers this is FIFO.

meyr_feeder.summary: Feeds captured sync samples into the N-pt FFT with one-shot FWD config.
meyr_feeder.header_comment:
meyr_feeder.v

Purely Pipelined FFT Feeder (No FSM)

ARCHITECTURE:
- One-shot config latch: fires config word immediately
after reset, latches done on acceptance. Does NOT block
the data path - just a single flip-flop.
- Data path: registered pass-through (1-cycle latency),
active as soon as config accepted.
- tlast counter: free-running, wraps every N samples.

meyr_ifft_peak_dut.summary: 2N-pt inverse FFT of R[m] and peak search -> integer CFO estimate.
meyr_ifft_peak_dut.header_comment:
meyr_ifft_peak_dut.v

PURPOSE:
Step 5: IFFT of R[m] -> time domain
Step 6: Peak power search -> integer CFO

ARCHITECTURE:
R[m] input -> xfft_IFFT (2N-pt, inverse, BFP) -> peak search

PEAK SEARCH (pipelined, matches C exactly):
power[i] = re[i]^2 + im[i]^2   (32x32 -> 64-bit, no overflow)
Track running max and its index.
After 2N bins: output best_idx and hw_cfo_int.

CFO CALCULATION (matches C):
if (best_idx < N)
hw_cfo_int = best_idx;
else
hw_cfo_int = best_idx - 2*N;

OUTPUTS:
ifft_tdata/tvalid/tlast : raw IFFT stream (for TB verification)
peak_idx                : index of maximum power bin
cfo_int                 : signed integer CFO estimate
cfo_valid               : pulses 1 cycle when peak search completes

frame_detector__T9c40.summary: Frame detection from the CP-autocorr metric: threshold + peak search -> frame start index.
frame_detector__T9c40.header_comment:
frame_detector (modular wrapper) — P3-12A refactor.

Architecture:
frame_detector (this wrapper)
├─ sample_power_sq       (combinatorial I^2+Q^2)
├─ sliding_window_sum    (registered ring-buffer rolling accumulator)
└─ frame_detect_fsm      (C reference Case1/Case2 detection FSM)

Pipeline stages (sample_valid → frame_found):
S_PROC (sample_valid=1) → posedge: SWS updates, window_valid registered
Next posedge: FSM sees window_valid, updates state; frame_found registered
Total: ~2 clock cycles from sample_valid to FSM state update.

After all search_len samples issued the wrapper holds in S_DRAIN for
DRAIN_CYCLES to allow the two-stage pipeline to settle, then exits.

Buffer read interface is unchanged from the monolithic design:
buf_rd_addr registered → data valid 1 cycle later (buf has 1-clock latency).
Each sample costs 2 wrapper clocks (S_FETCH + S_PROC).

Port interface is identical to the previous monolithic frame_detector.v;
frac_cfo_frame_corrector_top.v requires NO changes.

complex_rotator.summary: Rotates a complex sample by an NCO phase (complex multiply by e^{j*phi}).
complex_rotator.header_comment:
complex_rotator: rotates an IQ sample by exp(-j*theta) using NCO sin/cos.

r_out[n] = r_in[n] * exp(-j theta[n])
= (I_in + j*Q_in) * (cos(theta) - j*sin(theta))

I_out = I_in*cos + Q_in*sin
Q_out = Q_in*cos - I_in*sin

Corresponds to apply_carrier_freq_offset() in receiver.c (CFO correction form).

Data convention (project standard):
tdata[15:0]  = I (in-phase)
tdata[31:16] = Q (quadrature)

sin_in/cos_in connect directly to nco_phase_gen sin_out/cos_out.
sincos_valid gates the B-side of the internal multiplier.

Internally wraps complex_mult_iq with CONJ_B=1:
A × conj(B) where B = (cos + j*sin) implements the (cos - j*sin) correction.

frac_cfo_estimator.summary: Fractional CFO estimator: CP-lag phase (Van de Beek style) via CORDIC atan2.
frac_cfo_estimator.header_comment:
frac_cfo_estimator: Reads the autocorrelation peak at peak_lag and computes
its phase angle via the internal cordic_atan2 instance.

Output: frac_phase = atan2(autocorr_Q[peak_lag], autocorr_I[peak_lag])
encoded as signed PHASE_WIDTH-bit: 0x7FFF = +π.

Timeline (CORDIC LATENCY=L):
posedge P   : S_IDLE → S_SEND (latch peak_lag_r); CORDIC tvalid driven high
posedge P+1 : S_SEND → S_WAIT (cnt=0); CORDIC pipe[0] captures data
posedge P+2..P+L: S_WAIT cnt increments; CORDIC pipeline propagates
posedge P+L+1 : S_WAIT cnt=L-1 → S_DONE; CORDIC output regs update simultaneously
posedge P+L+2 : S_DONE reads stable CORDIC output; asserts frac_phase_valid, done; → S_IDLE

Total latency start→frac_phase_valid: L+2 clocks (default 17 with L=15).

frame_detect_fsm.summary: Frame-detect state machine: arming, threshold crossing, peak qualification windows.
frame_detect_fsm.header_comment:
frame_detect_fsm: C reference frame detection semantics only.

Implements exactly:
if first_window_energy <= thresh_mult:   # Case 1
scan forward for hit_count consecutive windows > thresh_mult
else:                                    # Case 2
skip windows until energy <= thresh_mult
then scan for hit_count consecutive windows > thresh_mult

Inputs come from sliding_window_sum (one pulse per complete window).
thresh_mult is pre-computed by the wrapper as threshold_in * window_len.

No sample power computation, no rolling accumulation, no buffer read logic.

FSM states:
IDLE          — waiting for clear deassertion and first window_valid
CHECK_FIRST   — classify first window as Case1 or Case2
CASE1_SCAN    — Case1: count consecutive above-threshold windows
CASE2_SKIP    — Case2: wait for energy to fall to or below threshold
CASE2_SCAN    — Case2: count consecutive above-threshold windows after skip
FOUND         — latch frame_index, assert frame_found
FSM_DONE      — one-cycle done pulse

frame_found and frame_index are stable from FOUND state until clear or reset.

nco_phase_gen.header_comment:
nco_phase_gen — synthesizable NCO: 256-entry Q1.15 sin/cos ROM + LATENCY-stage pipeline.
Replaces the behavioral $sin/$cos model from Step 20.
ROM: index = phase_acc[31:24] (8 MSBs), full 2pi cycle, 256 entries.
Convention: 0x7FFF=+1.0, 0x0000=0, 0x8001=-1.0 (Q1.15).
Phase: acc[31:24]=0x40→90°, 0x80→180°, 0xC0→270°.
Latency: LATENCY pipeline registers, same as behavioral model.

sliding_window_sum.summary: Sliding-window running sum over a fixed window.
sliding_window_sum.header_comment:
sliding_window_sum: rolling energy accumulation window.

On each sample_valid pulse:
- Appends sample_power to a circular ring buffer (depth = window_len).
- If window not yet full: accumulates sum, increments fill counter.
- Once window full: subtracts oldest entry, adds new entry (true sliding).
- Asserts window_valid for one cycle after each sample once the window is full.
- window_start_addr = sample_addr_in - window_len + 1 (monotonic scan assumed).

Parameters:
POWER_WIDTH    per-sample I^2+Q^2 width  (default 33)
ENERGY_WIDTH   accumulator width          (default 40)
ADDR_WIDTH     sample address width       (default 12)
MAX_WINDOW     maximum supported window   (default 64, ring buffer depth)

No Case1/Case2 logic, no frame detection, no buffer read logic.

timing_sync_top.summary: Timing synchronization: streaming CP autocorrelation metric + peak/frame detection.
timing_sync_top.header_comment:
timing_sync_top: Schmidl-Cox CP timing synchronization.

Frozen-architecture module instantiating streaming_cp_autocorr and
peak_detector (streaming argmax).

Metric: Manhattan |P_I[47:16]| + |P_Q[47:16]| — matches working algorithm
from timing_frac_cfo_top so peak_lag is consistent.

The SCA fires out_valid permanently from the first avg_pi_stb onward,
including for the initial CP_LEN-1 partial-window outputs.  Only outputs
with sca_sample_index >= STREAM_OFFSET correspond to full windows (physical
lag 0..NSC-1).  peak_detector is gated to receive only full-window samples;
its 0-based peak_index maps directly to physical lag.

FSM: S_IDLE → S_STREAM → S_DONE

iq_frame_buffer__Ad_DB2000.header_comment:
IQ frame buffer: captures one AXI-Stream IQ frame into a reg-array memory
and provides random-access read and write-back ports for downstream stages.

Write sources (mutually exclusive; wb_en takes priority):
1. AXI-Stream fill:  sequential writes from address 0, address auto-increment.
Activated by capture_start.  Terminates on s_axis_tlast or when the last
address is written (full condition).  s_axis_tready is deasserted when
wb_en is high or when the buffer is full.
2. Write-back (wb_*): explicit address, used by complex_rotator during CFO
correction to overwrite samples with corrected values.  May be used at
any time regardless of busy/full state.

Read port: synchronous registered output, 1-clock latency.
rd_data is updated when rd_en=1; holds last value otherwise.

Constraints:
DEPTH must equal 2^ADDR_WIDTH.
wb_en and capture_start must not be asserted in the same clock.

Parameters:
DATA_WIDTH  Width of each sample word (default 32 = {Q[31:16], I[15:0]})
ADDR_WIDTH  Address width; DEPTH = 2^ADDR_WIDTH (default 12 → 4096 entries)
DEPTH       Memory depth; must be 2^ADDR_WIDTH

cordic_atan2.summary: Vectoring-mode CORDIC atan2: 14 truncating micro-rotations + atan LUT -> Q1.15 phase.
cordic_atan2.header_comment:
cordic_atan2: Synthesizable pipelined CORDIC atan2 for HIL (hardware) build.

Computes phase = atan2(Q, I) encoded as Q1.15 signed fixed-point:
0x7FFF = +π, 0x8000 = -π, 0x0000 = 0
value = round(atan2(Q,I) / π × 32768), clamped to [-32768, 32767]

AXI-Stream interface: always-ready slave, LATENCY-cycle latency from
valid input to valid output.

Instantiated by frac_cfo_estimator:
tdata = {autocorr_Q[31:0], autocorr_I[31:0]}  (64-bit, Q in upper half)
tdata output = frac_phase [PHASE_WIDTH-1:0]

SYNTHESIS PATCH — 2026-06-05

Original behavioral implementation used non-synthesizable constructs:
real I_r, Q_r, angle_r;     — 'real' type: not synthesizable
$itor($signed(...))         — Synth 8-280: expression must be constant
$atan2(Q_r, I_r)            — simulation-only system function
$rtoi(angle_r / π * 32768)  — simulation-only system function

Replacement: pipelined CORDIC vectoring mode (integer shifts + adds only).
Stage 0          : quadrant normalization (ensure x > 0 for convergence)
Stages 1..LAT-1  : CORDIC micro-rotations, N_ITER = LATENCY-1 iterations

Accuracy: < 1 LSB error at N_ITER=14 (LATENCY=15). All arithmetic is
signed integer; no floating-point, no real types, no $itor/$atan2/$rtoi.

streaming_cp_autocorr.summary: Streaming cyclic-prefix autocorrelation P[n] over a CP_LEN window at lag NSC.
streaming_cp_autocorr.header_comment:
P2-02 (refactored P2-08b): Streaming sliding-window CP autocorrelation
Uses legacy primitives from rtl/phase2_legacy/:
delay_sample      — NSC-sample RAM delay
complex_mult      — 3-cycle pipelined complex multiply
moving_avg_optimized — CP_LEN-window sliding sum (x2 for P_i/P_q, x1 for E)
sample_power_sq   — 2-cycle |x|² computation
complex_to_mag    — alpha-max-beta-min magnitude (debug internal path)

Phase2 IQ convention: s_data[15:0]=I, s_data[31:16]=Q
Legacy modules expect upper=I, lower=Q — convention-handled in wiring below.

Pipeline: delay_sample(1cy) → complex_mult(3cy) → moving_avg(4cy) = 8cy total
Energy path: sample_power_sq(2cy) + 2cy align-delay → moving_avg(4cy) = 8cy total

complex_mult_iq__CC1.header_comment:
complex_mult_iq: 2-cycle pipelined AXI-Stream complex multiplier.

Computes A × B (or A × conj(B) with CONJ_B=1, etc.)
IQ packing: tdata[COMPONENT_WIDTH-1:0] = I, tdata[DATA_WIDTH-1:COMPONENT_WIDTH] = Q

Result arithmetic (for CONJ_A=0, CONJ_B=0):
I_out = (Ia*Ib - Qa*Qb) >> SHIFT
Q_out = (Ia*Qb + Qa*Ib) >> SHIFT

For CONJ_B=1 (used by complex_rotator for A × conj(B)):
I_out = (Ia*Ib + Qa*Qb) >> SHIFT
Q_out = (Qa*Ib - Ia*Qb) >> SHIFT

TWO-cycle latency (P5-04 timing pipeline cut):
Cycle 1: multiplier stage — register p_II / p_QQ / p_IQ / p_QI
Cycle 2: adder + shift + output register
This breaks the DSP chain (mult → add → shift → register) that
previously needed 2 cascaded DSP48E2 stages combinationally,
targeting 250 MHz on xczu9eg.

peak_detector__M21_C9.summary: Peak detector over a metric stream with qualification window.
peak_detector__M21_C9.header_comment:
Streaming unsigned argmax with start/done control protocol.

Scans a sequence of METRIC_WIDTH-wide unsigned values (one per clock
while data_valid=1) and reports the index and value of the maximum.
Tie-break: first occurrence wins (strict > comparison).

Control protocol:
- Pulse start=1 for one clock to begin a new scan.  The module latches
max_count on the same edge and clears all internal state.
- Feed data_in/data_valid/data_last.  data_last terminates the scan on
the clock it is accepted (data_valid && data_last).
- done pulses high for exactly one clock after the last value is accepted.
- peak_index and peak_value are stable from done until the next start.

Constraints:
COUNT_WIDTH >= INDEX_WIDTH
max_count <= 2^COUNT_WIDTH - 1; set to 0 to disable the overflow check.

Error (sticky, cleared only by aresetn):
- start asserted while busy
- data_valid without data_last after count reaches max_count (when max_count != 0)
